comments.value:
I'm still seeing "Mesh Disabled" bug happen in some capacity, as well as in some worlds for distant OR out-of-view(frustum culled) avatars. I want to add data that can hopefully help get it fixed. Or if this helps others with the bug & want to know if it can be prevented(& what else was tried). 

Seems like the risk is when the "primary" gameobject is disabled. AKA the one referencing the visemes in the vrcsdk for the avatar. Having a 2nd gameobject cannot fully help it, but it was a good tip to reduce likelihood of a disappearance!

What's happening? I believe if the bounding box of the "primary" gameobject gets completely culled OR disabled at any point in an animation on the avatar(or due to world behavior). If the primary gameobject is not visible to remote players when a Disabling event happens then the animations/visemes on the avatar stop updating, including important animations that can re-enable your primary mesh. A large bounding box helps so you are less likely to be culled when out-of-view, or if you have 2 gameobjects(i.e. cube suggested by the OP) & are careful with timing to never disable both at once during animations. Then visemes are what's most likely to break instead. Distant or out-of-view players may still find you without Mesh, or visemes/animations disabled when they come back.

Note: Bug ONLY happens for remote players, difficult to test alone. Reset needed to re-show avatar, OR coach others to re-enable avatar with hide/unhide safety setting.

Other things tried: Shrinking the non-primary gameobject Small so its never fully disabled. Sadly small gameobject if World Frozen now suffers from Occlusion Culling based on its origin point(now often in the floor). When resized big using an animation that object will flicker in and out of view annoyingly if the author has baked Occlusion Culling into the world. Frustum culling still can break you if the Primary gameobject gets disabled TOO. It was frustrating so I feel was worth mentioning!

This can reliably be seen in this world where the game mechanic makes everyone on the game field be very distant, especially if you are the Sniper during gameplay or sometimes when you use the Sniper practice:

https://vrchat.com/home/world/wrld_06c991da-951b-4ca5-b7d2-e3f5a9839e28/info

Upon end of game, all or most character visemes are now no longer updating, since during gameplay they may have been culled out of your view.

This also seems to happen on avatars that have a mechanic to hide/disable the body in favor of revealing a secondary effect. The primary Body GameObject is hidden, and NOT done using a shader. Typically when done by disabling the Body gameobject (specifically the gameobject associated with the Visemes and VRCSDK-associated stuff), but seems to be bounding box in-view dependent. 

I have seen the "Body Disappears bug" very occasionally happen with this avatar: 

https://vrchat.com/home/avatar/avtr_dacc17c3-d553-4517-881b-53bd968e9c4c 

Note: I do not know how this avatar is setup but it does have a spawn-in effect with particles and a disappearing effect where the body is hidden somehow, likely through disabling the Body mesh.

To repeat it as the avatar wearer, use the animations that hide the body and travel out of view of everyone, in certain cases or distances the avatar will need hidden and re-shown or the wearer will have to reset it. To repeat it as a remote player, be far enough away that you are outside of the character's bounding box and don't look while the animations are happening. Late joiners also will occasionally find you as invisible on arrival if the animation hiding the body was activated sometime before they arrive. Not sure the exact conditions that cause that, but I have found my friend whom uses this avatar often to be invisible and needs to be hidden/shown with the menu to see them.

I have seen the visemes not reactivate on the Body on this avatar when culled: 

https://vrchat.com/home/avatar/avtr_7b2adc2c-f6ef-4ad8-b9a2-f678b72bf7f8

Note: I personally worked on this avatar & learned about this bug through this feedback post as well as through testing to try to get the Body to stop fully disappearing for others. I could only get it to do so by making the bounding box larger-than-needed(but still Medium rated). Its possible there are still conditions where the primary body gameobject will be culled, but it happens less likely now that the timing is better on the animation and the bounding box was enlarged.

To repeat the bug as the avatar wearer: Drop the TV gameobject in the world and then "inhabit tv" this will make the Primary body mesh be disabled and put the character mesh into the TV, which is in a fixed position. You can freely walk around the world while this body mesh is disabled, including traveling far away. When you come back to view of Remote players there is a likelyhood your visemes will not play for those remote players if your bounding box was far enough to be culled during this time away.

During testing, the Primary body would also disappear until I carefully programmed the animation keyframes to not happen at the same point in the timeline on the finished version posted above.

 

I have a few test versions of this avatar with some of the behavior I am describing, this was during a time when the keyframes enabled/disabled the body on the same point in the timeline.

(these will not be public forever, but I will leave the avatar IDs in my account for reference to those who can internally use it)

https://vrchat.com/home/avatar/avtr_a971fe16-b2cc-48aa-b7cf-b4a1495ec2cb

https://vrchat.com/home/avatar/avtr_33789941-c4cc-4e71-a744-a749e3c7b798

Using "inhabit TV" out of view directly triggers the bug most reliably for remote users.

(sorry about additional flickering this was before we redid UVs) it was a wip after all.

details:
1. Make a VRChat avatar with Mesh Renderers

2. Make a menu animation to disable the gameobjects holding the Mesh Renderers (not just the Mesh Renderers) so the avatar becomes invisible

3. Start VRChat and ask some players to witness the animation

4. For you as a local player everything works fine, but for the distant players the gameobjects does not re-enables

A fix to this issue is to place an empty cube in the avatar scaled down to almost zero, but this lowers the performances rank
title: Avatar breaks for distant player but not locally when all gameobjects with Mesh Renderer are disabled
